record_type_quote:
Dubois, Rucker, and Galinsky (2012, Experiment 1) found that consumers view larger-size
options as a signal of higher status.

targets.authors: Dubois, D., Rucker, D. D., & Galinsky, A. D.
targets.title: Super Size Me: Product Size as a Signal of Status.
targets.evidence_quote:
In this replication report, we
present a preregistered direct replication of the first
experiment in Dubois et al. (2012), which tested the
primary hypothesis that choosing larger sizes in a
set of food options is associated with greater status
but does not significantly influence other dimensions that are not related to status such as perceived
niceness, honesty, or attractiveness.
targets.outcome_quote:
In this work, we failed to replicate the first experiment from Dubois et al. (2012), which found that
consumers associated larger portion choices with
higher status.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors state an overall failure to replicate Experiment 1.

reasoning: New independent sample directly re-tests a published finding; discussion supplies an explicit overall failure verdict.
